title: The Hanfu Renaissance
synopsis: Traditional hanfu dress is undergoing a revival among young people in China.

fullText.simplified:
汉服复兴

    如果让你想象一个汉朝的人，你觉得会是什么样的？毫无疑问，汉朝的人不会穿着T恤和牛仔裤。那他们会穿什么呢？如果你说：“他们穿汉服。”那我得说，你真了解中国。
    我们现在说的汉服，其实并不是指“汉朝的衣服”。五千多年前，中国还没有国王，中国人就已经有了自己的衣服。理论上，这些衣服都可以称为“汉服”。
    那为什么秦朝的衣服不叫“秦服”，唐朝的衣服不叫“唐服”，却都要叫汉服呢？这和“汉人”、“汉字”、“汉语”是一样的。汉朝是中国历史上第一个持久的、统一的朝代，持续了几百年。因此，人们就认可了自己是“汉人”，穿“汉服”。
    汉朝没有扣子和拉链，但你只需要把右边的衣襟拉到左边，打个结，再把左边的衣襟拉到右边，打个结，这样就穿好啦！
    汉朝的汉服，大致分成三种：
    第一种，“上衣下裳”相连，也叫“深衣”。
    这种衣服文雅又庄重，看起来特别有气质。贵族们不分男女，大部分时间都穿这个。普通老百姓也会在重要的日子穿上它。它好比现在的“连衣裙”，是上下连着的一整件衣服。汉朝的男人和女人，都可以穿这种“连衣裙”哦！
    第二种，“上衣下裳”分开。
    如果你是一个时尚达人，想要自己搭配衣服，那么这一种汉服就很适合你。它和现代的女性职业套装差不多，你可以选一件白色的上衣，再搭配一条绿色或粉色的裙子。
    如果你觉得太朴素，别急！汉服材料多种多样，有便宜的棉布汉服，有华丽的丝绸汉服，还有像云一样轻飘飘的纱衣。汉朝的时候，我们已经有了“扎染”，可以在衣服上印出各种各样的图案，譬如波点、条纹。如果你很爱美，我们还有手工刺绣：花草、虫鱼、鸟兽，什么都可以绣上去。
    第三种，“襦裙”。
    襦裙的种类就太多啦。上衣长短不一定，有从胸口往下都是裙子的，有从腰往下都是裙子的；外套样式也不一定，有左边压住右边的，有从中间敞开的……这种衣服更加美丽、新颖，虽然男女都可以穿，但更受女孩儿们的欢迎。
    到现在，中国的很多年轻人也喜欢穿汉服，希望能振兴汉服，让它拥有和T恤、牛仔裤同样的地位。为了完成这种“汉服复兴”，他们积极参加聚会，穿着汉服拍照、逛街，甚至穿去上学、上班。你有没有见过穿汉服的年轻人呢？
fullText.traditional:
漢服復興

    如果讓你想像一個漢朝的人，你覺得會是什麼樣的？毫無疑問，漢朝的人不會穿著T恤和牛仔褲。那他們會穿什麼呢？如果你說：“他們穿漢服。”那我得說，你真瞭解中國。
    我們現在說的漢服，其實並不是指“漢朝的衣服”。五千多年前，中國還沒有國王，中國人就已經有了自己的衣服。理論上，這些衣服都可以稱為“漢服”。
    那為什麼秦朝的衣服不叫“秦服”，唐朝的衣服不叫“唐服”，卻都要叫漢服呢？這和“漢人”、“漢字”、“漢語”是一樣的。漢朝是中國歷史上第一個持久的、統一的朝代，持續了幾百年。因此，人們就認可了自己是“漢人”，穿“漢服”。
    漢朝沒有釦子和拉鏈，但你只需要把右邊的衣襟拉到左邊，打個結，再把左邊的衣襟拉到右邊，打個結，這樣就穿好啦！
    漢朝的漢服，大致分成三種：
    第一種，“上衣下裳”相連，也叫“深衣”。
    這種衣服文雅又莊重，看起來特別有氣質。貴族們不分男女，大部分時間都穿這個。普通老百姓也會在重要的日子穿上它。它好比現在的“連衣裙”，是上下連著的一整件衣服。漢朝的男人和女人，都可以穿這種“連衣裙”哦！
    第二種，“上衣下裳”分開。
    如果你是一個時尚達人，想要自己搭配衣服，那麼這一種漢服就很適合你。它和現代的女性職業套裝差不多，你可以選一件白色的上衣，再搭配一條綠色或粉色的裙子。
    如果你覺得太樸素，別急！漢服材料多種多樣，有便宜的棉布漢服，有華麗的絲綢漢服，還有像雲一樣輕飄飄的紗衣。漢朝的時候，我們已經有了“扎染”，可以在衣服上印出各種各樣的圖案，譬如波點、條紋。如果你很愛美，我們還有手工刺繡：花草、蟲魚、鳥獸，什麼都可以繡上去。
    第三種，“襦裙”。
    襦裙的種類就太多啦。上衣長短不一定，有從胸口往下都是裙子的，有從腰往下都是裙子的；外套樣式也不一定，有左邊壓住右邊的，有從中間敞開的……這種衣服更加美麗、新穎，雖然男女都可以穿，但更受女孩兒們的歡迎。
    到現在，中國的很多年輕人也喜歡穿漢服，希望能振興漢服，讓它擁有和T恤、牛仔褲同樣的地位。為了完成這種“漢服復興”，他們積極參加聚會，穿著漢服拍照、逛街，甚至穿去上學、上班。你有沒有見過穿漢服的年輕人呢？

sentences.simplified: 到现在，中国的很多年轻人也喜欢穿汉服，
sentences.traditional: 到現在，中國的很多年輕人也喜歡穿漢服，
sentences.pinyin: dào xiàn zài zhōng guó de hěn duō nián qīng rén yě xǐ huan chuān hàn fú

sentences.simplified: 希望能振兴汉服，让它拥有和T恤、牛仔裤同样的地位。
sentences.traditional: 希望能振興漢服，讓它擁有和T恤、牛仔褲同樣的地位。
sentences.pinyin: xī wàng néng zhèn xīng hàn fú ràng tā yōng yǒu hé T xù niú zǎi kù tóng yàng de dì wèi
sentences.english: Nowadays, many young Chinese people also like wearing hanfu.

sentences.simplified: 为了完成这种“汉服复兴”，他们积极参加聚会，
sentences.traditional: 為了完成這種“漢服復興”，他們積極參加聚會，
sentences.pinyin: wèi le wán chéng zhè zhǒng hàn fú fù xīng tā men jī jí cān jiā jù huì
sentences.english: They hope to revive the hanfu and give it the same status as t-shirts and jeans.

sentences.simplified: 穿着汉服拍照、逛街，甚至穿去上学、上班。
sentences.traditional: 穿著漢服拍照、逛街，甚至穿去上學、上班。
sentences.pinyin: chuān zhe hàn fú pāi zhào guàng jiē shèn zhì chuān qù shàng xué shàng bān
sentences.english: In order to accomplish this “hanfu renaissance”, they actively participate in gatherings.

sentences.simplified: 你有没有见过穿汉服的年轻人呢？
sentences.traditional: 你有沒有見過穿漢服的年輕人呢？
sentences.pinyin: nǐ yǒu méi yǒu jiàn guò chuān hàn fú de nián qīng rén ne
sentences.english: They wear hanfu while taking pictures, going shopping, and even when going to school or work.

sentence_translations: The Hanfu Renaissance
If you were to imagine a person from the Han Dynasty, what would you think they were like?
There is no doubt that people from the Han Dynasty did not wear t-shirts or jeans. Then what did they wear?
If you say, “they wore hanfu”, then I must say that you are really knowledgeable about China.
The hanfu that we talk about now actually does not refer to “clothes worn during the Han Dynasty”.
Over 5,000 years ago, before there were kings in China, Chinese people already had their own clothes.
In theory, these clothes can all be called “hanfu”.
Then, why are clothes from the Qin Dynasty not called “qinfu”, and clothes from the Tang Dynasty not called “tangfu”?
Why are they all called hanfu?
The concept is the same as that of “Han people”, “Han characters”, and “Han language”.
The Han Dynasty was the first long-lasting, unified dynasty. It lasted several hundred years.
Therefore, people recognized themselves as “Han people”, and wore “hanfu”.
Hanfu do not have buttons or zippers.
But all you need to do is pull the right lapel over to the left and tie a knot, ..
.. then pull the left lapel over to the right and tie another knot.
Then you’re done!
The hanfu of the Han Dynasty are roughly divided into three types:
For the first type, the “upper and lower garments” are connected. It is also called the “shenyi”.
This type of clothing is elegant and dignified and looks especially classy.
The nobles, regardless of gender, would wear this type of clothing the majority of the time.
Ordinary people would also wear it on special occasions.
Similar to today’s ”one-piece dress”, the upper and lower parts are connected into a single garment.
Both men and women of the Han Dynasty could wear this type of “one-piece dress”!
For the second type, the “upper and lower garments” are separate.
If you are a fashionista and want to put together your own outfits, then this type of hanfu is perfect for you.
It is similar to the suits worn by female professionals today.
You can choose a white top and pair it with a green or pink skirt.
If you think this is too plain, don’t worry!
Hanfu come in many materials.
There are cheap cotton hanfu, gorgeous silk hanfu, as well as mesh clothing that is as light as a cloud.
During the Han Dynasty, we already had “tie-dye”. Various patterns, such as dots and stripes, could be printed on clothes.
If you enjoy dressing up, we also have hand embroidery:
Flowers and plants, insects and fish, birds and animals, anything can be embroidered onto the clothing.
The third type is the “ruqun”.
The are so many different types of ruqun. The length of the top can vary.
Some ruqun are skirt from the chest down, and some are skirt from the waist down.
The style of the jacket also varies. Some wrap left over right, and some are open in the middle …
This type of clothing is even more beautiful and original.
Even though both men and women can wear it, it is more popular among women.
Nowadays, many young Chinese people also like wearing hanfu.
They hope to revive the hanfu and give it the same status as t-shirts and jeans.
In order to accomplish this “hanfu renaissance”, they actively participate in gatherings.
They wear hanfu while taking pictures, going shopping, and even when going to school or work.
Have you ever seen young people dressed in hanfu?
